resources.string: Lets AURA read the screen and perform taps and gestures on your behalf, so it can drive apps that have no API. Every tap or text entry is Tier 3: AURA asks for your explicit approval each time, showing the exact action before anything happens. Text captured from the screen is treated as untrusted data and can never trigger an action by itself.
Tier 3 actions waiting for your explicit approval. Silencing this channel means those requests time out and are denied.
The ongoing connection to your AURA server. Low priority; keeps the device reachable for commands.
Notifications AURA posts on your behalf (reminders, task results, automation output).
The orb\'s state, and a tap to talk.
The address you reach jarvis-core on over LAN or WireGuard. Plain http is accepted only for private addresses, and only for the hosts listed in res/xml/network_security_config.xml.
Create it in the AURA console. It is stored on this device only, is excluded from backups, and is never sent anywhere but your server.
Shown on the server when this device registers. Device id: %1$s
Android gives third-party apps no low-power hotword path, so always-on detection means a genuinely open mic and real battery cost.

Off, the microphone streams continuously to your server, which does the detecting — everything the room says, all the time. On, the phone decides for itself and nothing is sent until you have said the name. The models are about 3.6 MB and come from YOUR server, not from the internet: AURA mirrors them so the phone never has to talk to anyone else.
Strict if the TV or a noisy room wakes it; eager if it misses you from across the room. Applies to detection on this phone.
Separate from the models above. The phone turns speech into text with a speech model it fetches from your server once (63 MB); the line below says whether it is here yet, and what leaves the phone.

AURA has an Android Auto screen — the orb, what you said and the reply — but a SIDELOADED build never appears in the car. Android Auto's "unknown sources" developer setting covers media, messaging and parked apps, and Google documents that it does not cover apps built with the Android for Cars App Library. This one is.

Two ways to see it: install from Google Play (an internal-testing track with one tester is enough — installing from Play is what makes the app a trusted source), or run the Desktop Head Unit on a computer and connect this phone to it, which is the supported way to develop against it. docs/how-to/android-auto.md has both.

Voice in the car is separate and is not affected: "Hey Aura" runs on this phone while Android Auto is connected, and the reply plays through the car's speakers over Bluetooth.

AURA can be told to answer only you. Enrolling teaches it what you sound like; whether it refuses anyone else is a setting on the server, so that turning on the thing which can refuse you is never a switch you hit by accident here.

Transcribing on this phone and "only my voice" cannot both be in force: the check runs on your server, on the sound, and a turn this phone transcribes sends words instead. Nothing is left to you — while the gate is enforcing, on-device transcription suspends itself and the line above says so. It cannot simply move here either: Android\'s offline recogniser owns the microphone and hands this app partial text and a level, never the audio.

These are in force. AURA asks this policy before it opens the microphone, and again whenever a headset or a car stereo connects, whenever you cross a geofence, and on the hour.\n\nA phone usually cannot tell whether it is at home. AURA only knows if you have a location automation whose geofence is called "home" — with one, "while at home" means what it says, and leaving the house stops the listening. Without one, being at home is treated as the answer, so the hours below are what decides: outside them nothing is listening unless you are in the car or wearing a headset. A window that wraps midnight (22 to 6) is fine.

A small pill on the camera hole while the assistant is on: its own core and whether it is listening. A conversation opens as the core alone at the bottom; once it goes to work it grows out of the pill on the camera, or stays at the bottom with the bottom switch on. It hides with the status bar when a video or game goes full screen. With the status switch it shows the time, network and battery instead. The system\'s own status icons stay beside it unless you turn on the cover: it needs the status switch and AURA car touchscreen turned on under Accessibility, hides the system\'s icons behind a band, leaves the corner where Android shows its camera and microphone dot open, and steps aside while the shade or the lock screen is down.

Only when the headset has a microphone of its own. AURA then captures through the phone\'s call path, where the hardware echo canceller stops it hearing its own reply two centimetres away — at some cost to transcription accuracy, which is why it is not the default. Keeping the mic open after a reply needs that canceller, so it does nothing on a route without one. The button never answers a confirmation prompt.

System check lists every permission and special access AURA can use, whether it is granted, and what stops working without it. None of them changes what tier an action is — they only decide whether it is possible.

Phone tasks are what THIS device does on its own — a geofence, a media button, a rule pushed to it. The house\'s automations live in the console\'s AUTOMATIONS tab, on this phone and in a browser alike.\n\nAPPROVALS is where you say which actions AURA may run without asking. The tier is the default and it is a good one; this is for the handful where you disagree with it.
The audit log records every action this device actually executed, with its tier and how it was authorised. Both it and the crash logs are local and yours.
Everything required is granted. %1$d optional item(s) are off.
Notifications are off. AURA cannot show you anything at all — not the wake word, not an approval waiting for your answer. Turn them on from System check, under Permissions.
Wake word: opens over whatever you are using. This is the good one — the orb is drawn directly, with no notification in the way.
Wake word: takes over the screen via a full-screen notification. Turn on DISPLAY OVER APPS as well for the orb to be drawn directly instead.

Wake word: arrives as a notification you have to TAP. Android will not let AURA put anything on screen by itself without DISPLAY OVER APPS above, or the full-screen grant in SYSTEM CHECK — on Android 14 the second is reserved for calling and alarm apps unless you grant it by hand.
Starts on its own: yes — battery exemption and overlay are both granted.
Starts on its own: yes — AURA is exempt from battery optimisation.
Starts on its own: yes — “display over other apps” covers it.

Starts on its own: NO. Android will not let AURA open the microphone after a restart without one of these. Until you grant one, a reboot leaves a notification you have to tap before “Hey Aura” works again.
On-device detection is ready (%1$.1f MB). Nothing reaches your server until you say the name.
Models are downloaded (%1$.1f MB) but detection is still on the server. Turn the switch above on to use them.
Models are NOT downloaded, so detection is still happening on the server — which means the microphone is streaming there continuously. Tap DOWNLOAD MODELS.
Models are not downloaded. About 3.6 MB, from your own server.
Speech is turned into text on this phone. The recording still goes to your server with the words, so it can check who is speaking; noise the phone hears no words in never leaves it.
The speech model is on its way from your server (63 MB, once); until it lands your server transcribes. Download models fetches it now.
Audio is streamed to your server, which transcribes it.
This handset: the microphone and wake word, its permissions, and which server it talks to.

Lets AURA turn touches on your car\'s screen into taps and swipes on this phone. It cannot read your screen content. It sees which app is in front, and only so it can stop showing your phone on the car when you close the app you opened.

AURA is also your car\'s Android Auto, with no Google app: the car screen shows AURA, maps, music, your apps, calls, messages and the car\'s own readings, and the steering-wheel voice button talks to AURA. Set up each car once, parked, with the car on and showing Android Auto. After that it connects on its own when you get in.
AURA needs the location permission. Grant it in the app on your phone.
Open AURA on your phone and point it at your server first.
AURA needs the microphone permission. Grant it in the app on your phone.
